A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PaTaRM and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Retained and relocated content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original PaTaRM evaluations on RewardBench and RMBench, downstream instruction-following experiments, rubric ablations, and scaling analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original PaTaRM results, including retained instruction-following experiments and new label-noise, mathematical reasoning, and runtime evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the format penalty for incorrect tags from -1.5 to -0.5. The central PAR mechanism, dynamic rubrics, and SFT-plus-GRPO pipeline remain. Replacing absolute margins with signed margins preserves their values on the indicator-selected reward branches.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 extends downstream coverage from instruction following to mathematical problem solving on GSM-8K and Math-500, with an additional training corpus. Section 5.1 introduces training scenarios with corrupted preference labels. The original preference-data sources and RewardBench, RMBench, IFEval, and InFoBench coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds same-data BT-Qwen3-8B/14B baselines and removes SynRM, Eurus-RM-7B, internlm2-7b-reward, and Deepseek GRM27B. Table 3 removes JudgeLRM. Appendix G.3 adds answer-correctness rule rewards as a comparator alongside Skywork, substantially revising the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes the stated reward-model RL budget from two epochs to one. Section 4.4 replaces separately trained pairwise variants with direct pairwise inference without additional training. New mathematical-policy experiments use 11,973 training samples and evaluation at step 96, with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-0.6B according to Tables 15–16. These are reported setting changes, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds preference-label-flipping robustness tests against BT-RM, computational-cost sensitivity analyses, and an additional generated-output case. The rubric ablation changes from six rows covering pointwise and pairwise training to one three-condition table, and reward-function training trajectories are revised. The SFT-only comparison is retained from v1 Table 1 in v2 Table 14.

E5.justification: V1 supplies no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. V2 Appendix G.1 and Table 13 report means and standard deviations over four independent random-seed runs for both model sizes, inference modes, and reward benchmarks. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes PaTaRM RewardBench/RMBench Overall scores from 82.5/73.6 to 84.3/78.7 for 8B and from 86.2/76.2 to 87.2/80.3 for 14B, alongside changed training settings. Pairwise, rubric-ablation, and voting results change; graded-reward margins now increase rather than decline. Noise, mathematical-policy, runtime, and pairwise RMBench results are added. Instruction-following results remain unchanged. V2 Tables 1 and 13 conflict on 8B Safety/Reasoning values.

T1.justification: Appendix A and Table 5 add an explicit forward-pass complexity argument: O(N) for scalar and pointwise scoring versus O(N log N) or O(N squared) for pairwise comparisons. The core PAR formulation is retained, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion raise the claimed average reward-benchmark improvement from 4.7% to 8.7%. The central contribution—pointwise generative reward modeling from pairwise preferences with adaptive rubrics—and the headline 13.6% downstream improvement remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations involving scalar-model data dependence, negative transfer, noise filtering through reasoning, and constant-reward hacking. It newly acknowledges dependence on preference-data quality and unverified explanation faithfulness. Appendix G.2 expands the interpretation of SFT as structural initialization, while the earlier discussion of inconsistent pointwise rubrics in Appendix E is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds runtime configurations, rollout and update counts, a 1024-token output-example limit, and peak-checkpoint reporting for rubric ablations. It removes pairwise SFT source-count columns and pairwise hyperparameter rows, and changes the code-access link from GitHub to an anonymous repository. Some new details conflict: Appendix D.3 specifies four rollouts while Table 10 lists sixteen.

R1.justification: V2 adds QA-lign by Dineen et al. and removes the JudgeLRM citation. Appendix A expands positioning around pairwise-data efficiency and pointwise inference complexity, while the main related-work taxonomy and most cited literature remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, and results discussion are extensively condensed or rewritten. Analyses move into a separate Section 5; Appendices B and G are reorganized; the LLM-usage appendix is replaced by architectural clarification. The author list and ethics wording also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, substantially resizes and relocates retained figures, reorganizes comparison tables, and converts case studies into colored panels. It adds noise plots and architecture, runtime, uncertainty, and mathematical-results tables. Reward-function plots are redrawn with an extended step axis; retained prompt figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, same-data BT controls and four-seed summaries make the central comparisons more informative; new robustness tests and runtime measurements better expose practical strengths and costs. However, removing the Deepseek pointwise-GRM comparison narrows relevant benchmarking, while inconsistent values in Tables 1/13 and rollout settings in Appendix D.3/Table 10 limit confidence in parts of the expanded evidence. The net quality gain is supported but qualified.
